key_insight: Combining molecular fragmentation, virtual QPU partitioning and half-qubit sampling reduces quantum simulation resources while preserving accurate molecular energies.
engineering_relevance: The framework enables parallel fragment execution and shallower circuits on current QPUs, reducing runtime and classical determinant-space demands.
method: Split molecular calculations into fragments using FMO.
Execute fragment circuits in parallel on virtual QPU regions.
Seed HCI expansion with half-qubit ansatz samples in FMO-QVM-HCI-HSQD.
evidence_signal: Tests on ibm_marrakesh and ibm_boston showed 39% lower two-qubit depth versus FMO-QVM-SQD and 82% less QPU time versus sequential FMO-SQD for the water trimer; the largest carmofur_Mpro calculation used 52 qubits and differed from FMO-HCI by 1.22 mHa.
watch_item: Resource savings depend on the system and comparison baseline; broader scalability beyond the demonstrated molecules and 52-qubit execution remains unestablished.
paper_title: Resource efficient Sample Based Quantum Simulation through Fragmentation and Virtual Partitioning of QPU
